jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
**Company Description**

Chooch helps build and run the best Computer Vision AI applications that make cameras intelligent, enhancing productivity & revenues, while reducing operational costs. Chooch has been named a leading computer vision platform by IDC.

**Role Description**

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer (US-based) to join our team. This is a full-time, hybrid role with frequent hands-on experience with customer projects in the Bay Area. The Machine Learning Engineer will be responsible for the successful design, accuracy, and backbone behind our Computer Vision AI applications. This includes data preparation, training, configuring neural networks, deploying networks in real customer locations, and refining computer vision algorithms for healthcare, manufacturing, and retail customers. This role requires frequent interaction with technical and non-technical customers while working closely within our solutions engineering teams. The Machine Learning Engineering role has opportunity to grow, lead technical projects, and improve current processes while providing meaningful feedback to our product and solutions teams.

**Product Description** Chooch AI is a computer vision platform that helps hospitals automate supply room monitoring and inventory management. Using fixed cameras and AI, the platform continuously tracks supplies in storage areas and updates on-hand counts in real time. When inventory levels fall below defined thresholds, replenishment orders are automatically generated and sent to ERP systems, eliminating manual counts and barcode scanning. Hospitals using Chooch AI significantly reduce critical stockouts, optimize inventory levels, and improve supply chain staff productivity. By turning supply rooms into self-managing systems, Chooch AI enables clinical and supply chain teams to focus more time on patient care.

Responsibilities/What you'll do at Chooch:

* Design, train and fine-tune models for object detection, classification, segmentation, tracking and anomaly detection on real customer video and images.
* Adapt pretrained and foundation models (YOLO-family detectors, ViTs, CLIP-style and vision-language models) to new customer use cases with limited labeled data.
* Own data pipelines end to end: curation, labeling guidelines, augmentation, synthetic data, and dataset versioning.
* Optimize models for production and edge hardware using quantization, pruning, distillation, ONNX export and TensorRT, hitting agreed latency and accuracy targets.
* Build evaluation suites with clear metrics (mAP, precision/recall, false-alarm rates per camera-hour) and catch regressions before release.
* Deploy and monitor models in production, diagnose drift and failure cases, and close the loop with retraining.
* Work with product, solutions engineers and customers to turn vague requirements into measurable model specs.
* Write clean, tested, reviewed code and contribute to shared ML tooling.

Nice to have

* Experience with vision-language models (CLIP, LLaVA-style models) or open-vocabulary detection.
* Multi-object tracking and video analytics (re-identification, action recognition, temporal models).
* Few-shot learning, active learning, or synthetic data generation for low-data domains.
* MLOps tooling: MLflow or Weights & Biases, Kubernetes, Triton Inference Server, CI/CD for models.
* Domain experience in Healthcare, retail and supply chain, manufacturing inspection, workplace safety or video surveillance.

Key Components

* Model Development and Optimization: Design, develop, and optimize machine learning models for computer vision applications.
* Data Management: Collaborate with ML engineers to ensure the collection, processing, and maintenance of high-quality datasets necessary for model training and testing.
* Algorithm Implementation: Implement state-of-the-art computer vision algorithms to improve system accuracy and performance in real-world scenarios.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely within the solutions engineering team to integrate machine learning models into the broader product and systems.
* On-Site Travel and Field Testing: Many of our projects are live deployments with major fortune 500 customers – testing new, innovative ML technologies. Traveling on site is sometimes needed to see the environment, test in the real-world, and ensure the technology is operating as expected.
* Performance Evaluation: Regularly evaluate the performance of computer vision models, using both qualitative and quantitative methods, and iterate to enhance accuracy and efficiency.
* Research and Innovation: Understanding of the latest developments in machine learning and computer vision, applying innovative approaches and technologies to solve complex challenges.
* Stakeholder Engagement: Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to understand their needs and translate them into effective technical solutions.
* Problem-Solving: Address and troubleshoot complex problems that arise during the development and deployment of computer vision systems.

The ideal candidate should be deeply passionate about machine learning and its real-world applications, particularly in improving and leveraging state-of-the-art neural networks to make an impact.

 **Requirements**  

* 3–5 years of industry experience building ML systems, with at least 2 years focused on computer vision.
* BS or MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Math or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Strong Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch (or TensorFlow) for training and debugging deep learning models.
* Shipped at least one computer vision model to production, and can explain the trade-offs made along the way.
* Solid grasp of CNN and transformer architectures for detection, segmentation and classification.
* Experience with OpenCV and image/video processing: decoding streams, preprocessing, augmentation.
* Working knowledge of model optimization for infere

**About Us**
------------

Witness AI invented intent-based AI security. While legacy tools monitor what users say to AI, we understand what they're trying to accomplish - stopping jailbreaks, data exfiltration, and shadow AI before damage occurs. We provide visibility into how employees and systems use AI - capturing prompts, responses, and agent activity - so security teams can monitor risk, investigate incidents, and enforce guardrails in real time.

------------

As a Machine Learning Engineer, you’ll design, build, and evaluate language models that power our AI security products. You’ll own the end-to-end pipeline — from dataset curation and preprocessing to experiment design, evaluation, and visualization of results. This role blends engineering and applied research, with an emphasis on producing reliable, interpretable, and safe language models.

------------------

* Build scalable pipelines to collect, preprocess, and manage datasets for training and evaluation of LLMs.
* Design and run experiments to evaluate LLMs on accuracy, robustness, fairness, and safety.
* Create dashboards, reports, and visualizations to communicate evaluation results, trends, and failure cases.
* Develop and leverage knowledge graphs to structure data, enrich evaluation, and improve context-driven model performance.
* Work with researchers to translate new ideas into engineering workflows, and with data scientists to automate QA checks and guardrails.
* Fine-tune, optimize, and integrate models into production systems with a focus on reliability, scalability, and monitoring and CI/CD best practices.
* Contribute to ML tooling and experimentation frameworks to accelerate iteration.

--------------------------

* **Experience:** 2–5+ years working in machine learning or data science, ideally in a security or infrastructure-heavy environment.
* **Technical Skills:**

* Contributions to open-source ML, NLP, or security projects.

We’re looking for an engineer to lead the optimization of OpenAI’s state-of-the-art frontier models on TPUs. You will own performance across the full forward pass, from model code through kernels to execution on the hardware.

You’ll have broad technical ownership: identifying performance bottlenecks, choosing the most impactful improvements, and carrying them through implementation and validation. We welcome experience gained through either training or inference, with a strong foundation in optimizing real workloads on TPUs.

* Optimize model execution on TPUsance across the complete forward pass and the interactions between model code, kernels, and hardware.

* Build benchmarks and tools to measure performance, validate correctness, and guide optimization work.

jobs.title: Research Scientist, Machine Learning
jobs.description:
Meta is seeking a Research Scientist to advance the state of the art in ads AI research. In this role, you will conduct original research in areas such as operations research, optimization, representation learning, time series forecasting, or generative modeling, with the goal of driving fundamental breakthroughs that power Meta's AI-driven ads product and beyond. You will work alongside researchers and engineers to translate novel findings into real-world impact at unprecedented scale.  
  
  

### **Research Scientist, Machine Learning Responsibilities:**

* Design and execute original AI research projects spanning areas such as deep learning architectures, optimization methods, and generative models
* Design optimization and forecasting methods for allocation planning and marketplace optimization
* Develop and validate novel algorithms and modeling approaches through rigorous experimentation, ablation studies, and statistical analysis
* Translate research findings into scalable implementations that can be integrated into production AI systems serving billions of users
* Define and instrument evaluation frameworks, benchmarks, and metrics to measure research progress and model quality
* Collaborate with cross-functional partners across engineering, product, and data science to align research directions with high-impact product opportunities
* Communicate research findings through internal technical reports, external publications, and presentations to both technical and non-technical audiences
* Mentor other researchers and engineers on the team, providing technical guidance and constructive feedback on research methodology and implementation
* Drive the technical roadmap for one or more research areas, identifying opportunities, building stakeholder alignment, and coordinating execution across teams
* Contribute to the broader research community through peer-reviewed publications, open-source contributions, and participation in academic and industry venues

  
  
  

### **Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience
* 2+ years of experience conducting machine learning research, including developing and evaluating novel models, algorithms, or training methodologies
* Experience publishing original research in peer-reviewed machine learning venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ACL, or equivalent
* Experience implementing and training large-scale machine learning models using frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow
* Experience designing experiments, selecting appropriate metrics, and drawing statistically sound conclusions from empirical results
* Experience communicating complex research findings in writing to both technical and non-technical stakeholders through papers, design documents, or technical reports
* Has obtained a PhD in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or relevant technical field

  
  
  

### **Preferred Qualifications:**

* Research experience in one or more specialized areas such as operations research, optimization, forecasting, multimodal learning, reinforcement learning, or generative modeling
* Demonstrated ability to identify high-impact research directions that align with long-term product or platform goals
* Experience mentoring other researchers and contributing to the technical growth of a research organization
* Track record of driving research from initial hypothesis through production deployment at scale, including collaboration with applied engineering teams

  
  
  

### **About Meta:**

Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. Apps like Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp further empowered billions around the world. Now, Meta is moving beyond 2D screens toward immersive experiences like augmented and virtual reality to help build the next evolution in social technology. jobs.title: Software Engineer - Realtime Pipeline
jobs.description:
**About Bridge Neurotech**
--------------------------

Bridge Neurotech is building a non-invasive functional ultrasound imaging (fUSI) platform with AI-based neural decoding for brain-computer interface applications. We are a seed-stage neurotechnology company developing technology that has the potential to transform how we interact with the human brain.

**About the Role**
------------------

We are looking for a Software Engineer - Realtime Pipeline to own the realtime system that runs from raw RF data off the probe all the way to decoded outputs from our neural decoding model — beamforming, imaging preprocessing, and ML inference, all in one tightly coupled latency budget. The inference latency budget is tightly coupled to the imaging pipeline latency budget: they share GPU, share memory, share the data stream. This role owns the entire realtime path and is accountable for it as one system.

Given the neural decoding model, you turn it into a production realtime decoder, sitting on top of the imaging pipeline you have also built. We build from open primitives like the Mach beamformer (https://github.com/Forest-Neurotech/mach), and you provide the technical leadership and strategy to mature the system — designing, developing, testing, deploying, and enhancing it into a scalable software solution — including what to extend, what to replace, and what to push upstream.

You will work closely with our ML/AI Lead on the model serving boundary, our Embedded Systems Engineer on the data handoff from the probe, our Imaging Scientist on the imaging pipeline itself, and our Applications Engineer on the decoded output handoff downstream.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* Own the end-to-end realtime path: raw RF data ingestion, beamforming, processing (e.g., clutter filtering), ML preprocessing, model inference, and decoded output.
* Build the ML inference engine: model loading from artifacts, GPU memory residency, batching, TensorRT/ONNX or hand-built CUDA inference, and kernel-level integration with the upstream imaging compute.
* Integrate, extend, and, where appropriate, contribute to GPU beamforming.
* Hit and hold realtime throughput and latency targets at multi-Gbit/s ingest with deterministic tail latency suitable for closed-loop decoding.
* Define and own the model serving contract with the ML/AI Lead and the path for model updates without service interruption.
* Build the streaming and storage layer that serves raw and processed data to both offline training and realtime inference.
* Collaborate with other team members to define the upstream interface to the device acquisition layer and the downstream interface to the BCI applications layer.
* Build observability into every stage and develop benchmarks and regression tests that lock in both pipeline performance and inference correctness as the system evolves.

**Who You Are**
---------------

**Required**

* BS/MS/PhD in computer science, electrical engineering, or a related field, with 8+ years building production realtime or HPC systems.
* Expert-level CUDA and modern C++; experience writing or extensively modifying GPU kernels for signal processing or imaging workloads.
* Demonstrated experience building production ML inference systems: taking trained PyTorch (or equivalent) models to deployment on GPUs under hard latency budgets. Hands-on with TensorRT, ONNX Runtime, Triton, or hand-built CUDA inference engines.
* Demonstrated experience building realtime data pipelines at multi-Gbit/s rates with tight latency budgets.
* Strong grasp of data structures, algorithms, and the signal processing stack relevant to imaging or RF: beamforming concepts, FFTs, IQ demodulation, SVD-based filtering, autocorrelation.
* Proficiency in Python and the PyTorch ecosystem sufficient to collaborate with the ML team, identify what needs to change for production, and have informed conversations about model architecture trade-offs that affect latency.

**Nice to Have**

* Experience with functional imaging or other high-data-rate imaging modalities.
* Experience integrating ML inference with upstream realtime compute, including shared GPU memory layouts and minimizing host–device round-trips.
* Experience with high-bandwidth I/O: GPUDirect Storage, RDMA, kernel-bypass networking, NVMe arrays.

**What We Offer**
-----------------

* The opportunity to shape a role and a team from the earliest stages.
* Direct collaboration with leading clinicians and neuroscientists at top-tier academic institutions.
* Excellent medical benefits and a 401(k) with 6% match.

Bridge Neurotech is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply.

**Full Stack Engineer**
=======================

**Efference** - Robust Robotic Perception

**Location**: North Beach, San Francisco, CA

**Employment** **Type**: Full Time

**Location** **Type**: On-site

**Department**: Engineering

**Company Overview**
--------------------

Efference builds robust, high-performance robotic perceptual systems that make robots easier to develop and faster to deploy. Our technology integrates proprietary optical designs, advanced sensor fusion, depth estimation, image sensor processing, and tightly optimized hardware-software stacks to enable reliable perception across general and specialized robotic systems.

We are currently deploying the first generation of vision systems with state-of-the-art hardware and software while actively prototyping generations two and three of our core perceptual system.

Efference was founded by Gianluca Bencomo, a PhD student at Princeton University whose research spans visual neuroscience, Bayesian filtering for fast and robust sensor fusion, neural network inductive biases, and robotics perception. The company is backed by Y Combinator and Anti Fund.

**Position Overview**
---------------------

As a Staff Full Stack Engineer, you will play a foundational role in shaping the software layer that connects Efference’s perception hardware to real-world robotic applications. You will own the design and implementation of end-to-end systems that enable remote device control, high-throughput data streaming, and scalable, cloud-based data collection and training workflows.

This role sits at the intersection of web, embedded systems, robotics, and cloud infrastructure. You will collaborate closely with embedded firmware, vision, and ML teams to ensure low-level perception capabilities are exposed through intuitive, reliable, and high-performance user-facing tools.

Your work will directly impact teleoperation, large-scale data collection, and on-device inference for modern robotics workloads, including visual SLAM, vision-language-action models, and lightweight diffusion-based policies.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Lead the UX and system architecture of web and mobile applications for controlling and monitoring embedded robotic devices.
* Design and implement WiFi- and Bluetooth-based communication pipelines for remote control, telemetry, and device management.
* Own backend services that support data ingestion, storage, and orchestration for robotics data collection and model training.

jobs.title: Compiler Backend Engineer
jobs.description:
**Normal Computing | Build with Us**
------------------------------------

Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), London, Copenhagen, and Seoul.

**The Role**
------------

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. Getting a model correct on that hardware is the frontend's job; making it fast is yours. Our hardware does not look like a CPU or GPU, so its compiler backend can't be borrowed from one. As a Compiler Engineer focused on the backend, you will help design and build the custom compilation that maps LLM inference onto it, from scheduling and memory planning to the code our hardware actually executes.

You will work at the boundary between the compiler and the hardware, closely enough to know when an optimization belongs at a different layer, or when the right answer is a new abstraction. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will measure your work against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, and against silicon as it arrives.

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

* **Code Generation**: Build the passes that turn lowered programs into the code our hardware executes, designing new compilation approaches where conventional ones don't fit. Success means correct, efficient code for every operation our models need.
* **Scheduling and Memory Planning**: Own how work and data are scheduled and placed across our hardware's resources, measured by utilization and end-to-end latency on LLM inference.
* **Fusion and Dispatch**: Own fusion and dispatch decisions for LLM inference, so the hardware spends its time computing rather than moving data.
* **Hardware Co-Design**: Work the abstraction layer between the compiler and the hardware, and feed compiler constraints back to our hardware architects while the design can still change.
* **Profiling and Validation**: Validate every optimization with measured results from simulators, FPGA prototypes, and then silicon, and maintain a performance regression suite the team trusts.
* **Cross-Team Handoffs**: Take lowered programs from our frontend compiler engineers, and decide with the team which operations the compiler generates and which use hand-tuned kernels.

**What Makes You a Great Fit**
------------------------------

* Deep experience with compiler optimization or code generation for accelerators or other non-CPU targets: scheduling, tiling, fusion, or resource allocation
* Comfort working close to hardware: you think in terms of memory bandwidth and utilization as well as asymptotic complexity
* Willingness to design compilation approaches from first principles when existing ones don't fit the hardware
* Track record of shipping optimizations that moved a measured performance number
* Comfort building software for hardware that is still evolving, from simulation through bring-up
* Fluency in Python, and familiarity with C, C++, or Rust

**Bonus Points**
----------------

* Experience with PyTorch's compilation stack (TorchDynamo, FX, Inductor, torch.export) or other ML compilers, such as IREE, TVM, or XLA
* Experience compiling for in-memory, spatial, or other non-von-Neumann compute targets
* Background in hardware design tools such as logic synthesis or place-and-route
* Experience building or using cycle-level or performance simulators to guide optimization decisions
* Contributions to open-source compiler or kernel infrastructure (e.g., PyTorch, Triton, TVM, MLIR, LLVM)
* Publishing or presenting compiler or performance work at venues such as MLSys, ASPLOS, or CGO

***Equal Employment Opportunity Statement***

*Normal Computing is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status.*

*Normal Computing is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please let us know at accommodations@normalcomputing.com.*

***Privacy Notice***

*By submitting your application, you agree that Normal Computing may collect, use, and store your personal information for employment-related purposes in accordance with our* *Applicant Privacy Notice**.*

**How many companies can say they’ve been in business for over 179 years?!**

Here at ZEISS, we certainly can! As the pioneers of science, ZEISS handles the everchanging environments in a fast-paced world, meeting it with cutting edge of technologies and continuous advancements. ZEISS believes that innovation and technology are the key to a sustainable future and solutions for global change. We have a diverse range of portfolios throughout the ZEISS family in segments like, Industrial Quality & Research, Medical Technology, Consumer Markets and Semiconductor Manufacturing Technology. We are a global company with over 42,000 employees and have over 4,000 in the US and Canada alone! Make a difference, come join the team!

  

**Location:** Dublin, CA

  

**What’s the role?**

The Software Engineer supports the development, automation, testing, and continuous improvement of manufacturing and engineering processes for advanced X-ray source products. This position combines software development, manufacturing automation, data analysis, and hands-on engineering support to improve production efficiency, product reliability, test capability, and data-driven decision-making.

The Software Engineer develops tools that automate production and test activities, acquires and processes engineering data, and provides analytical capabilities to characterize product performance and reliability. Working closely with manufacturing, test, reliability, and engineering teams, the role may also support production equipment and X-ray source testing as needed.

**Sound Interesting?**

**Here’s what you’ll do:**

**Software Development & Manufacturing Automation**

* Design, develop, test, and maintain software tools that automate manufacturing, engineering, and production-test processes.

* Develop automated data-acquisition solutions for collecting engineering and production information from test equipment.

* Develop scripts and utilities for processing large quantities of production and test data.

* Improve existing automation by increasing execution efficiency, reducing manual operations, and enabling parallel data-processing activities where appropriate.

* Develop methods for organizing and correlating production data, test results, product history, operating hours, and component serial-number information.

* Support the development and implementation of production and final-test automation, including automated acquisition of vacuum, emitter, and heater metrics.

**Production Test & Engineering Support**

* Support engineering and manufacturing teams with the execution and troubleshooting of production-test processes.

* Operate and support automated and semi-automated test equipment used for X-ray source conditioning, calibration, characterization, and final verification.

* Assist with high-voltage conditioning, emitter testing, focus and spot calibration, astigmatism correction, randomizer testing, droop verification, write-to-flash operations, and other production-verification activities.

* Monitor test progress, identify abnormal conditions, and troubleshoot issues encountered during source testing.

* Document source status, test conditions, anomalies, and completed manufacturing and test operations.

* Work directly with engineers and manufacturing personnel to support products through the production-test sequence, including Doghouse and Versa testing.

**Engineering Data Analysis**

* Develop software for analyzing production, calibration, reliability, and product-performance data.

* Aggregate and analyze data from multiple products, test stations, and historical production records.

* Develop filtering and data-cleaning methods that distinguish valid production results from failed or non-representative test data.

* Perform statistical analysis of product characteristics and manufacturing trends, including spot-size performance across products and operating energies.

* Generate engineering datasets, plots, summaries, and other analytical outputs used to support technical decisions.

* Support engineers in evaluating product performance across operating conditions and product populations.

**Reliability & Root-Cause Investigation Support**

* Develop data-collection and analytical tools that support product-reliability investigations.

* Correlate component serial numbers with manufacturing history, operating hours, production results, field information, and test data.

* Support engineering investigations through automated acquisition and analysis of source and component performance data.

* Prepare structured datasets for additional statistical analysis using engineering analysis tools such as JMP.

* Assist engineers in identifying patterns and relationships among manufacturing history, component configuration, and observed product behavior.

**Production & Process Improvement**

* Identify opportunities for software and automation to reduce repetitive manual activities and improve manufacturing efficiency.

* Support the development and improvement of automated production workflows.

* Assist with integrating software tools into manufacturing and engineering environments.

* Maintain clear documentation for software tools, data-analysis methods, test activities, and production status.

* Collaborate with engineering and manufacturing teams to improve the traceability and accessibility of production data.

jobs.title: Validation & Tooling Software Engineer, Residential Energy Products
jobs.description:
**What to Expect**

The Tesla Energy Device Software team is looking for a Software Engineer to design and maintain the internal tooling and simulation infrastructure that lets residential energy firmware teams move faster with higher confidence. You will work across Powerwall, Backup Gateway, Wall Connector, and related home energy products—building Software-in-the-Loop (SIL) environments that approach real-world behavior, and the visualization and debugging tools that make complex multi-process systems understandable.

Device software is only as good as the feedback loop around it. Our goal is tooling that shortens the path from idea to validated behavior: high-fidelity SIL, field-trace capture and replay, rich reports and dashboards, control-flow and system visibility, and extensible instrumentation (traces, hooks, probes). As products, revisions, capabilities, and regional variants grow—including market-specific configurations such as external companion hardware—you will regularly extend the platform so new and existing products can be brought into the same validation and debugging workflow.

 **What You'll Do**

* Design, implement, and maintain internal SIL, harness, and developer tooling (primarily Python and Go) that improves correctness, debuggability, and release confidence for residential energy device software
* Build and evolve close-to-real-life SIL environments for multi-process embedded Linux systems; close gaps between simulation and field behavior where they matter most
* Develop visualization and debugging tools—including report generation, SIL-driven dashboards, control-flow visualization, and related analysis views—so engineers can understand system behavior without spelunking logs alone
* Implement and support trace/hook/instrumentation systems that reach into device software (Go, Rust, C/C++); enable capture of traces in the field and faithful replay in SIL
* Onboard new products, product revisions, capabilities, and regional or market-specific configurations (e.g. installations that require additional external hardware) into shared tooling and SIL workflows
* Collaborate with Product, Device Software, Hardware, and Validation to turn team pain points into clear tool designs, tests, and shippable internal platforms
* Improve reliability and usability of tooling used daily by engineers; reduce time-to-root-cause for lab, SIL, and field issues
* Contribute to automated tests, CI integration, and engineering practices that raise product reliability, developer productivity, and release confidence
* Support production and fleet needs where tooling helps: bring-up, field anomaly reproduction, and continuous improvement after launch

  
**What You'll Bring**

* Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or equivalent experience
* Ability to multi-task, prioritize, and work in an extremely fast-paced, collaborative environment
* Experience building internal developer, validation, or simulation tooling that other engineers rely on day to day
* Proficiency in languages used for tooling and integration—Python, Go; Rust, C, or C++ experience is a plus for working close to device software and multi-process systems
* Comfort working across the boundary between tools and the systems under test: embedded or device software, multi-process Linux, IPC, logs, and traces
* Real-world experience in one or more of: Software-in-the-Loop (SIL), simulation harnesses, or high-fidelity test environments for embedded or multi-process systems; Debug, visualization, or observability tooling (dashboards, report generators, timeline/control-flow views, or similar); Trace, instrumentation, capture/replay, or hook-based systems for reproducing field or lab scenarios offline; Extending test or simulation platforms to support new products, hardware variants, or regional configurations
* Strong software fundamentals: clear interfaces, maintainability, failure handling, and testability—tooling is product software for internal users
* Experience with unit / integration automation, CI pipelines, or HIL-style validation adjacent to SIL is a plus
* Experience with Docker and QEMU (or similar container and machine emulation tooling) is a plus for packaging, isolation, and realistic SIL environments
* Exposure to complex embedded Linux systems, home energy / battery / inverter products, multi-device site setups, or market-specific product variants is a plus

#### **Benefits**

Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:

* Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
* Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
* Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
* Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
* Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* 401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
* Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
* Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
* Employee Assistance Program
* Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
* Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
* Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
* Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
* Tesla Babies program
* Commuter benefits
* Employee discounts and perks program
* Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)

  

#### **Expected Compensation**

$140,000 - $300,000/annual salary + cash and stock awards + benefits

**About Us**
------------

At Rigetti, our mission is to build the world’s most powerful computers to solve the world’s most challenging problems. Rigetti is a pioneer in superconducting Qubits and full stack quantum computing systems. In addition to introducing the first multi-chip quantum processor, Rigetti has led the way in software systems for quantum computing, with a distributed operating environment for hybrid quantum-classical computing, and a state-of-the-art streaming characterization and measurement development and execution platform

### **Role Overview**

We're hiring a Network & Infrastructure Engineer to own hands-on networking and physical infrastructure work across our Berkeley and Fremont sites, including our fabrication facility and quantum labs, while also supporting our AWS cloud environment and infrastructure-as-code practices. This is a hybrid role by design: the person in this seat is expected to flex between traditional network/data center work and cloud infrastructure/DevOps work as priorities shift.

Our network is unusually complex for a company our size: an AWS-backed cloud platform, redundant connectivity, a fabrication facility with its own segmented security environments, and labs full of specialized equipment. We're expanding lab and fab space and scaling up our fleet of quantum systems, so you'll be building new infrastructure, not just maintaining what's here. This is a local role with no additional travel required.

The ideal candidate brings deep, hands-on expertise in on-site networking and infrastructure and real capability in AWS, infrastructure-as-code, and Kubernetes. That combination lets this person understand requirements from both sides and translate between them without a hand-off. * Apply Infrastructure-as-Code practices (Terraform, Ansible, or similar) to provision and manage infrastructure repeatably.
* Support CI/CD pipelines and automation workflows that touch infrastructure delivery.
* Support containerized workloads (Kubernetes/Docker) where they intersect with infrastructure provisioning and networking.

**General**

* Follow detailed internal procedures to ensure work is performed accurately, consistently, and safely.
* Flex between network/physical infrastructure work and cloud/DevOps work based on shifting business priorities — this role is not siloed to one discipline.
* Growth area (nice-to-have, not required): as expertise develops, recommend purchase orders, work directly with vendors, and help guide technical requirements for infrastructure buildouts.

**Networking & Physical Infrastructure**

* 5–8+ years of hands-on experience with physical infrastructure such as servers, racks, switches, patch panels, cabling, PDUs, and related data center or lab hardware.
* 5–8+ years of experience with networking concepts and troubleshooting, including TCP/IP, VLANs, DNS, DHCP, routing, switching, firewalls, and network security principles.
* 5+ years of experience working with Arista, Cisco, Palo Alto, Meraki, Raritan, APC, or similar networking and infrastructure platforms.
* Experience installing, configuring, upgrading, or troubleshooting physical servers, network devices, or infrastructure systems.
* Ability to work on-site and provide physical infrastructure support at both Berkeley and Fremont locations.

jobs.title: Software Engineer, Research Tooling
jobs.description:
Engineering · Full-time · Palo Alto, CA

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.
  
  
SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

### **About the role**

As a Software Engineer on the Research Tools team, you'll build the infrastructure and applications that enable our researchers to iterate quickly, run complex experiments, and extract insights. This is a full-stack product-engineering role.

You'll work directly with researchers and engineers to deeply understand their workflows, identify bottlenecks, and rapidly ship solutions that multiply their productivity. Whether you're creating platforms for experiment orchestration, developing novel visualization tools for model evaluation, or building abstractions for understanding model behavior at scale, your work will directly accelerate our mission of building frontier AI models.

We're looking for someone who can jump into new problems, quickly develop domain expertise, and independently drive impactful projects from conception to delivery. No prior ML or research experience is required.

### **What you’ll do**

* Build and maintain the full-stack applications and infrastructure researchers rely on daily, covering experiment setup, feedback collection, and results analysis.
* Own complete product areas from user needs through design, implementation, and iteration, setting standards for how to build research applications.
* Create reusable platforms and tools that speed up new research applications, then prototype, ship, and iterate quickly based on real-world usage.
* Partner with research teams to turn their workflows and pain points into intuitive interfaces and abstractions that make complex research tasks fast and approachable.

### **You may be a fit if**

* You’ve had experience building tools, platforms, or infrastructure for technical users (engineers, researchers, data scientists, analysts, etc.)
* You’ve shipped full-stack products and owned systems from user interface to storage or services, using technologies such as TypeScript and React alongside Node, Python, or Go.
* You’ve built dense, data-facing tools such as transcript viewers, diffing systems, review queues, observability products, or operational dashboards—and you have strong opinions about how structured data should be rendered.
* You have strong product instincts, can identify the right problems to solve, and can move from concept to working prototype with ease.
* You move quickly under ambiguity, collaborate closely with researchers and domain experts, and take open-ended problems from rough need to reliable product.

### **ing**

**Location:** Remote, Full-time

The Children’s Tumor Foundation (CTF) is not a traditional research foundation. We operate as a patient-centered drug discovery engine for NF, a group of genetic conditions that cause tumors to grow on nerves affecting 1 in 2,000 individuals. We operate by accelerating the full continuum of scientific discovery, from basic research through translation to clinical trials and approved treatments — while empowering patients and building the financial infrastructure to support that journey. We catalyze progress by uniting academia, industry, regulators, and patient advocates around shared goals.

**General Summary**

The Biomedical Data Scientist will drive CTF’s efforts to turn neurofibromatosis (NF) data into actionable insights for drug discovery, positioning the Foundation as a leader in NF data. Working closely with CTF’s Science teams, this role integrates research, clinical and publicly available data to identify and prioritize therapeutic opportunities across NF1, *NF2*-related schwannomatosis, and non *NF2*-related schwannomatosis. The Biomedical Data Scientist will also work closely with vendors to steward CTF’s NF data ecosystem, lead CTF’s AI-enabled research resource for the NF community, and share data and findings with the broader research community. The ideal candidate is a self-starter with strong technical skills in bioinformatics, data integration, analysis, and visualization, strong writing skills, and a passion for advancing NF research.

**Principal Duties and Responsibilities**

* NF Data Ecosystem Stewardship: Serve as CTF’s subject matter expert for the NF Data Portal and associated analysis platforms. Work with data vendors and external data partners to track data sharing plans and milestones, identify new data sources, and ensure the quality, integrity, accessibility, and reuse of NF datasets. Manage subscriptions to various platforms.
* Data-Driven Target Discovery: Lead integrated analyses of genomic, molecular, clinical, imaging, and publicly available datasets to identify, prioritize, and validate therapeutic targets for NF. Work closely with CTF’s Drug Scout and Preclinical Initiatives teams and with NF researchers to translate findings into therapeutic hypotheses, target recommendations, and opportunities for preclinical validation. Create clear visualizations and summaries that inform CTF’s research recommendations.
* AI-Enabled Research: Evaluate and apply emerging AI and computational approaches to accelerate NF data integration and hypothesis generation. Serve as administrator of CTF’s Anthropic (Claude) workspace for the NF community, leading its build-out by surfacing NF datasets, publications, and sample analyses, managing access, and gathering user feedback.
* Community Engagement and Dissemination: Represent CTF and collaborate with Key Opinion Leaders to author peer-reviewed publications and present findings at conferences. Implement and manage data science workshops and platform sessions at the NF Conference, contribute to open-source tools and resources for the NF research community, and promote NF data sharing and reuse. Additional duties as required.

* MS in Data Science, Ph.D. preferred – Computational Biology, Bioinformatics, or a related field.
* 1-3 years experience in working with public and/or private datasets and large-scale data repositories.
* Strong expertise in data management, analysis, and visualization techniques.
* Experience implementing Claude Science or comparable AI research platforms, including using AI agents for literature review, data analysis, and reproducible computational workflows.
* Demonstrated understanding of, and adherence to, HIPAA regulations and data privacy standards.
* Proven track record of scientific publications and presentations.
* Familiarity with open-source tool development and collaborative research environments.
* Ability to work both independently and within a multidisciplinary team.
* Excellent communication skills.
* Strong organizational skills are needed, which reflect the ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks seamlessly with precise attention to detail.
* Creative and analytical thinker.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience integrating multi-omic and clinical datasets for therapeutic target identification and prioritization.
* Experience applying machine learning, AI, or large language model (LLM) tools to biomedical research questions.
* Experience analyzing clinical, real-world, or patient registry data, including patient-reported outcomes.
* Familiarity with neurofibromatosis or rare disease research.

**Preferred Skills:**

* Programming: R and/or Python, Linux command line, cloud computing
* Omics Analysis: bulk and single-cell RNA-seq, WGS/WES, proteomics, and methylation
* Therapeutic Target Discovery Resources: pathway and network analysis, multi-omic integration, and experience with public resources like GEO, TCGA, GTEx, DepMap, ChEMBL, and Open Targets
* Machine Learning and AI: Claude Science or other LLM-based platforms, experience with agentic AI like Claude Code
* Data Visualization and Reporting: ggplot2, matplotlib, Shiny

jobs.title: Systems Software Engineer, Hardware Validation
jobs.description:
**Systems Software Engineer, Hardware Validation**

**About us:**

Voyant Photonics builds silicon photonic chips that steer and switch light at high speed. They power next generation, chip-scale FMCW LiDAR for robotics and autonomy, and optical circuit switches (OCS) for AI data centers. Based in NYC, we’re a hands-on team designing, building, and deploying frontier hardware to solve problems that matter, from how machines see to how AI scales.

**About the role**

Our tech stack spans FPGA and ASIC logic, microcontroller firmware, Linux drivers and cross platform user-facing APIs, and every layer changes every week. We're hiring engineers, at more than one level, to keep them integrated, tested and releasable.

**What Actually Matters**

Code is cheaper to write than ever. Knowing what should be written, and what "done" means, is the job. We want someone with strong, well-reasoned opinions about how software should be organized and how test coverage should grow, who argues for them, and who changes their mind when the evidence says so.

Things we believe in as a team:

* **Fix it at the source.** A bug gets fixed where it lives, even when that's someone else's code. The friction of working in each other's areas is worth it.
* **Live at the tip.** Every repo tracks the latest of everything it depends on. Small, frequent bumps surface breaks while they're still cheap to fix.
* **Duplicated code is broken code.** Two copies drift apart, and then one of them is wrong.
* **It doesn't work until someone else has run it on hardware.** Your own simulation or bench is where you start, not where you're done.

Disagree with one? Tell us why when you apply.

**What You'll Do**

* Own releases from commit to customer: build, verify, version and ship product bundles (FPGA bitstreams, firmware, drivers, APIs), including field updates, with release notes and runbooks people trust.
* Grow our HIL CI to cover every subsystem, and bring each new product into it from its first bring-up board.
* Track every bug CI finds to its root cause, whether that's Python, Rust, firmware, a Linux driver or FPGA logic, then fix it.
* Take our products into the systems that use them: time sync, calibration, sensor fusion, and open-source ecosystems like OCP and ROS.

**What We're Looking For**

* 2+ years of software engineering experience, or equivalent depth from research, internships or serious personal projects. We'll scale scope to experience.
* Strong Python, and comfort debugging languages you don't write every day.
* Hands-on hardware experience: bring-up, reading schematics, and using lab instruments to tell a software bug from a board bug.
* CI/CD experience, ideally against real hardware.
* Proactive communicator who cares about documentation to support cross functional team members & customers.

**Nice to Have**

* Rust, C++ or embedded C (we use STM32)
* Linux device drivers, especially SPI and custom low-level interfaces
* Reading System Verilog well enough to debug across the FPGA boundary
* HIL rigs and lab automation (SCPI/VISA, self-hosted CI runners)
* Timing and signal-integrity debug across SPI, I2C, UART, Ethernet and JTAG/SWD, plus board rework
* Fiber optics and optical test equipment
* Datacenter networking, PTP, point clouds or ROS 2
* Supporting software that external customers depend on

**What You'll Gain**

* Ownership of the release and test architecture for our products, from first bring-up to shipping: real decisions, not someone else's pipeline.
* Close collaboration with hardware, optics, signal processing and perception engineers, and real influence over technical direction at an early-stage company.
* A path toward customer-facing integration work, if that interests you.

**Life at Voyant**

We build frontier hardware & software from our lab and office in Midtown Manhattan, where optical tables, lab benches and electronics sit alongside traditional office space. Our work is hands-on and primarily in person, but we don’t run on a rigid 9-to-5. We partner with customers across time zones, so some calls start early or run late, and we adjust schedules around them. We run a high-trust, high-accountability environment: you’ll own meaningful work, move quickly and often wear more than one hat. Voyant provides catered lunch every day at HQ, and we’re a diverse group of food lovers from around the world who enjoy sharing food, culture and technical ideas around the lunch table.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

Voyant Photonics is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, pregnancy, marital or partnership status, age, national origin, citizenship, veteran or military status, disability, medical condition, genetic information, caregiver status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Compensation Range: $110K - $170K

new_jobs.title: Machine Learning Engineer
new_jobs.description:
**Company Description**

Chooch helps build and run the best Computer Vision AI applications that make cameras intelligent, enhancing productivity & revenues, while reducing operational costs. Chooch has been named a leading computer vision platform by IDC.

**Role Description**

We are looking for a Machine Learning Engineer (US-based) to join our team. This is a full-time, hybrid role with frequent hands-on experience with customer projects in the Bay Area. The Machine Learning Engineer will be responsible for the successful design, accuracy, and backbone behind our Computer Vision AI applications. This includes data preparation, training, configuring neural networks, deploying networks in real customer locations, and refining computer vision algorithms for healthcare, manufacturing, and retail customers. This role requires frequent interaction with technical and non-technical customers while working closely within our solutions engineering teams. The Machine Learning Engineering role has opportunity to grow, lead technical projects, and improve current processes while providing meaningful feedback to our product and solutions teams.

**Product Description** Chooch AI is a computer vision platform that helps hospitals automate supply room monitoring and inventory management. Using fixed cameras and AI, the platform continuously tracks supplies in storage areas and updates on-hand counts in real time. When inventory levels fall below defined thresholds, replenishment orders are automatically generated and sent to ERP systems, eliminating manual counts and barcode scanning. Hospitals using Chooch AI significantly reduce critical stockouts, optimize inventory levels, and improve supply chain staff productivity. By turning supply rooms into self-managing systems, Chooch AI enables clinical and supply chain teams to focus more time on patient care.

Responsibilities/What you'll do at Chooch:

* Design, train and fine-tune models for object detection, classification, segmentation, tracking and anomaly detection on real customer video and images.
* Adapt pretrained and foundation models (YOLO-family detectors, ViTs, CLIP-style and vision-language models) to new customer use cases with limited labeled data.
* Own data pipelines end to end: curation, labeling guidelines, augmentation, synthetic data, and dataset versioning.
* Optimize models for production and edge hardware using quantization, pruning, distillation, ONNX export and TensorRT, hitting agreed latency and accuracy targets.
* Build evaluation suites with clear metrics (mAP, precision/recall, false-alarm rates per camera-hour) and catch regressions before release.
* Deploy and monitor models in production, diagnose drift and failure cases, and close the loop with retraining.
* Work with product, solutions engineers and customers to turn vague requirements into measurable model specs.
* Write clean, tested, reviewed code and contribute to shared ML tooling.

Nice to have

* Experience with vision-language models (CLIP, LLaVA-style models) or open-vocabulary detection.
* Multi-object tracking and video analytics (re-identification, action recognition, temporal models).
* Few-shot learning, active learning, or synthetic data generation for low-data domains.
* MLOps tooling: MLflow or Weights & Biases, Kubernetes, Triton Inference Server, CI/CD for models.
* Domain experience in Healthcare, retail and supply chain, manufacturing inspection, workplace safety or video surveillance.

Key Components

* Model Development and Optimization: Design, develop, and optimize machine learning models for computer vision applications.
* Data Management: Collaborate with ML engineers to ensure the collection, processing, and maintenance of high-quality datasets necessary for model training and testing.
* Algorithm Implementation: Implement state-of-the-art computer vision algorithms to improve system accuracy and performance in real-world scenarios.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely within the solutions engineering team to integrate machine learning models into the broader product and systems.
* On-Site Travel and Field Testing: Many of our projects are live deployments with major fortune 500 customers – testing new, innovative ML technologies. Traveling on site is sometimes needed to see the environment, test in the real-world, and ensure the technology is operating as expected.
* Performance Evaluation: Regularly evaluate the performance of computer vision models, using both qualitative and quantitative methods, and iterate to enhance accuracy and efficiency.
* Research and Innovation: Understanding of the latest developments in machine learning and computer vision, applying innovative approaches and technologies to solve complex challenges.
* Stakeholder Engagement: Collaborate with internal and external stakeholders to understand their needs and translate them into effective technical solutions.
* Problem-Solving: Address and troubleshoot complex problems that arise during the development and deployment of computer vision systems.

The ideal candidate should be deeply passionate about machine learning and its real-world applications, particularly in improving and leveraging state-of-the-art neural networks to make an impact.

 **Requirements**  

* 3–5 years of industry experience building ML systems, with at least 2 years focused on computer vision.
* BS or MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Math or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* Strong Python and hands-on experience with PyTorch (or TensorFlow) for training and debugging deep learning models.
* Shipped at least one computer vision model to production, and can explain the trade-offs made along the way.
* Solid grasp of CNN and transformer architectures for detection, segmentation and classification.
* Experience with OpenCV and image/video processing: decoding streams, preprocessing, augmentation.
* Working knowledge of model optimization for infere

As an Applied Scientist on the Sponsored Products and Brands Off-Search team, you will contribute to the development in Generative AI (GenAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) to revolutionize our advertising flow, backend optimization, and frontend shopping experiences.
